history.summary: One of India's finest brick temples, built entirely of red brick and dedicated to Vishnu (named Lakshman/Lakshmana, traditionally after Rama's brother). Commissioned by queen Vasata (Vastadevi), wife of Panduvamshi king Harshgupta (mother of Mahasivagupta Balarjuna), in memory of her husband, c. 7th century CE. Panchayatana style: garbhagriha, antarala and a ruined mandapa; the sanctum entrance has a beautifully carved stone doorframe with Vishnu reclining on Shesha, plus Krishna Leela and Vaishnava dwarapala carvings in Gupta–post-Gupta style. ASI-maintained with an adjacent museum; entry fee reported as Rs 20–25 (Indian) / Rs 300 (foreign) — reports vary, verify. Sirpur (ancient Shripura/Sripura), on the Mahanadi in Mahasamund district, was the capital of Dakshina Kosala (5th–12th c.), yielding 22 Shiva temples, 5 Vishnu temples, 10 Buddhist viharas and 3 Jain viharas. CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the district/town name 'Mahasamund' — corrected to Chhattisgarh; actual town is Sirpur.

name: Sirpur Lakshman Temple
town_description: Sirpur (ancient Shripura/Sripura) is a historic town on the banks of the Mahanadi in Mahasamund district, Chhattisgarh, about 82 km from Raipur. Capital of Dakshina Kosala from the 5th to 12th century CE, it is a multireligious archaeological site — Hindu temples, Buddhist viharas and Jain viharas side by side — being prepared for a UNESCO World Heritage bid, with ASI museums on site.

travel.road: On NH 53, ~82 km from Raipur and ~37 km from Mahasamund town; regular bus services connect Raipur and Sirpur
